intents.name: Memory Hierarchy Optimization
intents.description: Restructure loop nests to maximize data reuse within each level of the CPU cache hierarchy (L1/L2/L3) and minimize costly main-memory accesses.
intents.rationale: Loop-nest computations with large working sets suffer severe performance degradation from cache misses. Multi-level blocking and data reorganization are the single most impactful optimizations for CPU loop nests on this hardware.

transformations.name: Tiling
transformations.description: Partition the iteration space into multi-dimensional blocks so that the working set of each tile fits within a target cache level.
transformations.rationale: Tiling creates temporal locality by ensuring that data loaded into cache is reused across multiple iterations before eviction, dramatically reducing memory bandwidth pressure.
transformations.action_template: Tiling(tile_sizes) — tile_sizes is a vector of integers with one entry per loop dimension; 0 means 'do not tile that dimension'. OR Tiling(loop_band, tile_sizes) — tile_sizes applies to the specified loop band.

transformations.name: Loop Interchange
transformations.description: Reorder the loops in a loop nest to change the iteration order without altering the computation's semantics.
transformations.rationale: Loop ordering determines memory access stride patterns; placing the dimension with stride-1 access innermost improves spatial locality and enables hardware prefetching.
transformations.action_template: LoopInterchange(loop_band, permutation) — permutation is a reordering of loop indices within the band. OR LoopInterchangeSwap(loop_band, adjacent_pair) — swap two adjacent loops in the nest.

transformations.name: Promotion
transformations.description: Copy a tile of data from its original location into a contiguous temporary buffer before computation and write results back afterward.
transformations.rationale: Promotion eliminates non-unit-stride accesses and cache conflict misses by ensuring tiles are stored contiguously, improving effective cache utilization and enabling aligned vectorized loads from packed data.
transformations.action_template: Promotion(operand_id) — promote the specified operand of the target operation to a local contiguous buffer. OR Promotion(operand_ids) — promote multiple operands simultaneously.

intents.name: SIMD and Instruction-Level Parallelism
intents.description: Exploit the processor's vector execution units (AVX2) and instruction pipeline to maximize floating-point throughput per core.
intents.rationale: Modern CPUs achieve peak throughput only when SIMD lanes are fully utilized and the FMA pipeline is kept busy; without vectorization and sufficient ILP, a core operates at a small fraction of its potential.

transformations.name: Vectorization
transformations.description: Map loop iterations to SIMD vector lanes, enabling multiple data elements to be processed by a single instruction.
transformations.rationale: AVX2 provides 4-wide FP64 (or 8-wide FP32) vector lanes; vectorizing the appropriate innermost loop dimension yields up to a 4x (or 8x) throughput improvement per core.
transformations.action_template: Vectorization(vector_sizes) — vector_sizes is a vector of integers specifying the SIMD width for each loop dimension; 0 means 'do not vectorize that dimension'. OR Vectorization(target_loop, vector_width) — vectorize a specific loop at the given width.

transformations.name: Unrolling
transformations.description: Replicate the loop body multiple times within a single iteration, reducing loop overhead and exposing more independent operations to the processor pipeline.
transformations.rationale: Unrolling increases instruction-level parallelism by exposing multiple independent FMA operations, enabling the out-of-order engine to fill pipeline bubbles and better utilize functional units.
transformations.action_template: Unrolling(target_loop, unroll_factor) — unroll the specified loop by the given factor. OR Unrolling(loop_band, unroll_factor) — unroll the innermost loop of the specified band.

intents.name: Coarse-Grain Parallelism and Loop Structure
intents.description: Distribute work across multiple CPU cores and restructure the iteration space to expose more regular, optimization-friendly loop patterns.
intents.rationale: With 28 physical cores available, utilizing thread-level parallelism is essential; additionally, restructuring irregular loop nests into canonical contraction forms enables more effective application of tiling, vectorization, and packing.

transformations.name: Parallelization
transformations.description: Distribute iterations of parallel (non-reduction) loops across multiple threads for concurrent execution on different cores.
transformations.rationale: Outer parallel loops in dense loop nests are independent and can be distributed across the 28 available cores for near-linear speedup, provided tiles are large enough to amortize synchronization overhead.
transformations.action_template: Parallelization(target_loop, num_threads) — parallelize the specified loop with the given thread count. OR Parallelization(loop_band, num_threads) — parallelize the outermost parallel loop in the band.

transformations.name: Kernel Lowering
transformations.description: Lower a structured high-level operation (e.g., convolution) into a canonical contraction loop nest via data layout transformations such as im2col.
transformations.rationale: Convolution loop nests have irregular sliding-window access patterns; lowering to a contraction form regularizes the iteration space and memory accesses, making subsequent tiling, vectorization, and packing significantly more effective.
transformations.action_template: KernelLowering() — lower the target structured operation to a contraction form with associated reshape operations. No parameters; the RL policy's action selection itself is the decision to apply this transformation.
